title: How many flags did the flower seller give away?
description: A flower seller gives one flag to every customer. Customers who bought only champak, only marigold, and both are counted with the letters p, q and r, and a customer who bought both flowers is counted once.
teaching_notes: One idea: the groups of customers do not overlap, and each customer gets one flag, so the numbers of customers are added once each. Watch for students who count the customers who bought both flowers twice.

video_script.why: A learner uses the method of counting each kind separately and adding: the groups of customers are written with letters and added.
video_script.substitution: The method of counting horizontal and diagonal matchsticks separately and adding, with groups of customers in place of the matchsticks.
video_script.anchor: a flower seller with three groups of customers: only champak, only marigold, and both
video_script.payoff_line: The flags given away are p plus q plus r

final_answer.spoken: p plus q plus r flags

never_show: the finished expression before the answer beat
maths_rules: one flag for every customer, so flags = customers
three groups of customers do not overlap: p, q, r
a customer who bought both flowers is one customer, so r counts once
check p = 3, q = 4, r = 2: 3 + 4 + 2 = 9 customers and 9 flags; p + q + 2r would give 11
video_script.design: One idea: every customer gets one flag, so the flags are the customers added once each. Assumes the example of counting kinds separately and adding. Three groups of customers stay on the stage.
open_questions: The book's seller is named Pushpita, who has no name slot in this chapter, so the video says a flower seller.

narration: <bookmark mark='p1'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='p2'/>On Independence day, a flower seller sells champak and marigold flowers.
<bookmark mark='p3'/>Some customers bought only champak, some bought only marigold, and some bought both. She gave a tiny flag to every customer.
<bookmark mark='p4'/>How many flags did she give away that day?

beats.on_screen: the flower seller and customers stay on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: three groups of customers labelled p, q and r ; one flag for each customer

marks.g1: the letters p, q and r are written on the three groups
marks.g2: one flag is drawn beside each customer

narration: <bookmark mark='g1'/>The letters p, q and r stand for the number of customers in the three groups.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>Every customer gets exactly one flag.

beats.on_screen: Given: p customers bought only champak ; q customers bought only marigold ; r customers bought both ; one flag for every customer

marks.gv1: p and q are written for the first two groups
marks.gv2: r is written for the group that bought both

narration: <bookmark mark='gv1'/>Given, p customers bought only champak, and q customers bought only marigold.
<bookmark mark='gv2'/>Also r customers bought both flowers. Every customer got one flag.

beats.on_screen: To find: the number of flags given away
narration: <bookmark mark='fd'/>We find the number of flags. We work the same way as the example in your book. Take each group on its own, and then add.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: one flag for each customer, so the flags = the number of customers

marks.s1a: an arrow joins each customer to one flag

narration: <bookmark mark='s1a'/>First, every customer gets one flag. The number of flags is the number of customers.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: the customers who bought both are r customers, each counted once

marks.s2a: the group r is marked with a single tick for each customer

narration: <bookmark mark='s2a'/>Second, a customer who bought both flowers is still one customer. That customer gets one flag, so the r customers are counted once.

marks.s3a: the three groups are joined with plus signs

narration: <bookmark mark='s3a'/>Third, the three groups do not overlap, so we add the numbers of customers in the groups.

beats.on_screen: Step 4, check with p = 3, q = 4, r = 2: 3 + 4 + 2 = 9 customers and 9 flags ; p + q + 2r would give 11

marks.s4a: 3, 4 and 2 replace p, q and r
marks.s4b: the extra count of the both group gives 11, which is too many

narration: <bookmark mark='s4a'/>Fourth, check with three, four and two customers in the groups. That is three plus four plus two, which is nine customers, so nine flags.
<bookmark mark='s4b'/>Counting the group that bought both twice would give eleven, which is too many.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The flags given away are p plus q plus r.
